rounds.proof_sketch: For input shape [16, 256, 256]: dim2=256, block_size=min(dim2,1024)=256, so threadIdx.x∈[0,255]. col=threadIdx.x, thus col∈[0,255]. Original guard: col>=256 is never true. Mutated guard: col>256 is never true. The difference (col==dim2=256) is unreachable since max(col)=255.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from 'col >= dim2' to 'col > dim2'. The only difference occurs when col == dim2. However, the kernel launch configuration sets block_size = min(dim2, 1024) = min(256, 1024) = 256. This means threadIdx.x ranges from 0 to 255, and since col = threadIdx.x, col can only take values in [0, 255]. Since dim2 = 256, the condition col == dim2 is never satisfied. Both the original condition (col >= 256) and the mutated condition (col > 256) always evaluate to FALSE for all threads, making the mutation semantically equivalent under this fixed shape.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shapes. Would require either dim2 > 1024 (so block_size caps at 1024 while dim2 is larger, leaving threadIdx.x=dim2 possible if dim2<=1024 edge case) or the ability to change shapes so dim2 < block_size, neither of which is permitted by the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: When implementing boundary guards in CUDA kernels, consider using assertions or static checks to verify that the guard condition is actually reachable given the launch parameters. This would help identify dead code paths and prevent equivalent mutations from being generated in mutation testing.
